c.tagline: Taiwan's ancient capital — temple town, historic forts, and street-food soul.

taxi.fareNote: Yellow taxis are metered and cheap and easy to hail in the center; Uber and local apps (LINE Taxi, yoxi) are also widely available.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police and 119 reaches fire and ambulance; the 24-hour multilingual tourist hotline 0800-011-765 helps foreign visitors.

hood_landmark.Anping District: Anping Old Fort Fort Zeelandia Tainan
hood_landmark.East District (Dong Qu): Blueprint Culture and Creative Park Tainan

hood_desc: The historic heart of Taiwan's oldest city, where Chihkan Tower, the Confucius Temple, and the lantern-lined Shennong Street sit among temples, teahouses, and street-food stalls; the best walkable base for sightseeing.

Tainan's original harbor district, home to Anping Old Fort (Fort Zeelandia), the Anping Tree House, sunset-facing seafood streets, and Old Street snacks; a must-see for history and coastal atmosphere.

The city's modern, youthful quarter around the universities, filled with cafes, boutiques, the Blueprint Culture and Creative Park, and the huge Garden and Dadong night markets; suits shoppers and night-market grazers.
The area around Tainan Railway Station and Tainan Park, a convenient transit gateway with mid-range hotels and easy bus links across the city; handy for arrivals and first nights.
A quieter, more residential and coastal stretch toward Golden Beach and the fishing harbors, away from the tourist crush; good for a relaxed, local-feeling stay.
lodging: Shangri-La Far Eastern Plaza Hotel Tainan

water.note: Tap water is treated but locals boil or filter it; drink boiled or bottled.

transit.hours: Tainan city buses run roughly 6:00 AM to about 10:00-11:00 PM with limited frequency on many routes; there is no metro or tram, so taxis and ride apps cover late nights.
transit.note: Tainan has no metro or tram — the city relies on an extensive but infrequent public bus network (free for the first 8 km with an EasyCard on many routes) plus the T-Bike public bicycle share for short hops; taxis and Uber fill the gaps.
transit.pay: Tap an EasyCard or iPASS stored-value card on buses and T-Bike (buy and top up at any convenience store); many city bus rides are free for the first 8 kilometers with a card. Cash is accepted onboard with exact change.

bus: Tainan Bus Station (Guoguang & Ubus intercity coaches)
train: Tainan HSR Station (Shalun, Taiwan High Speed Rail to Taipei)

transit.m: City bus (Route 5 / Red Line) to Tainan Railway Station (~20 min)
Taxi or Uber to city center (10-15 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Taiwan; a 10% service charge is sometimes added at hotels and upscale restaurants, but street stalls and taxis expect no tip.

food.name: Danzai noodles
food.desc: Small bowl of thin noodles in a light shrimp-and-pork broth topped with minced pork, a prawn and often a braised egg. Tainan's signature.

places.name: Du Hsiao Yueh
places.note: The founding house of danzai noodles, cooking them since 1895.

places.name: Small Park Danzai Noodles
places.note: Michelin Bib Gourmand pick, often called the city's best bowl.

places.name: Chihkan Danzai stalls
places.note: Old-town stalls serving the same bowl for a fraction of the price.

food.name: Coffin bread
food.desc: A thick slab of bread deep-fried, hollowed out and filled with creamy chicken, seafood or curry stew, then lidded like a little coffin.

places.name: Chikan Coffin Bread
places.note: Michelin-listed stall widely named the best coffin bread in Tainan.

places.name: Flower Night Market stalls
places.note: Several vendors sell it hot on Thursday, Saturday and Sunday nights.

places.name: Kangle Market food court
places.note: The dish was invented in this market; rival stalls sit side by side.

food.name: Milkfish soup and congee
food.desc: Tainan's farmed milkfish served as clear belly soup or rice congee in milkfish broth, with pepper, ginger and fried shallots. A local breakfast.

places.name: Milkfish King
places.note: Famous specialist for milkfish congee and belly soup.

places.name: Yongtong Milkfish Congee
places.note: Local favourite; go early, they sell out by mid-morning.

places.name: Guohua Street breakfast stalls
places.note: Row of old stalls serving milkfish and rice dishes from dawn.

food.name: Shrimp rolls
food.desc: Fresh shrimp and fish paste bound with vegetables, wrapped in caul fat and deep-fried into crisp cylinders eaten with wasabi soy.

places.name: Chou's Shrimp Rolls
places.note: Family recipe fried since 1965; the reference version in Tainan.

places.name: Anping Old Street stalls
places.note: Several long-running vendors along the old street sell them hot.

places.name: Guohua Street stalls
places.note: Central alternative if you are not heading out to Anping.

food.name: Eel noodles
food.desc: Sea eel flash-fried then tossed with thick noodles in a sweet-sour, slightly smoky sauce. Fast wok cooking, eaten in minutes.

places.name: Fu Sheng Hao Eel Noodles
places.note: Long queues at this market institution for eel noodles and squid.

places.name: Yongle Market food stalls
places.note: Dense cluster of veteran stalls; easy to graze several dishes.

places.name: Guohua Street stalls
places.note: More eel and squid noodle shops within a short walk.

food.name: Tofu pudding
food.desc: Silky douhua in brown sugar syrup with peanuts, red beans, taro or tapioca. Tainan claims it as the birthplace of the dessert.

places.name: Tong Ji Anping Tofu Pudding
places.note: The best-known Anping shop; queues form all afternoon.

places.name: Anping Bean Jelly
places.note: Family recipe said to date to the Qing dynasty; very smooth texture.

places.name: Guohua Street dessert stalls
places.note: Central stalls serving douhua hot in winter, iced in summer.

food.name: Winter melon tea
food.desc: Winter melon slow-boiled with sugar into a dark caramel block, then dissolved in water and served over ice. Tainan's default cold drink.

places.name: Yi Feng Winter Melon Tea
places.note: Century-old shop still boiling its own winter melon blocks.

places.name: Guohua Street drink stalls
places.note: Cheap cups to carry while eating your way down the street.

places.name: Yongle Market stalls
places.note: Handy stop between the eel noodle and shrimp roll counters.

food.name: Sugarcane and fruit juice
food.desc: Pressed sugarcane, guava, papaya milk and ai-yu jelly with lemon, all made to order from southern Taiwan fruit. Sold at every night market.

places.name: Flower Night Market
places.note: Tainan's biggest night market; dozens of juice and ai-yu stands.

places.name: Garden Night Market drink stalls
places.note: Fresh-pressed cane and fruit milks alongside the food rows.

places.name: Yongle Market juice stalls
places.note: Daytime option for sugarcane and guava juice in the old town.

landmarks: Anping Old Fort (Fort Zeelandia)
The 1624 Dutch stronghold that birthed Taiwan's oldest city, its weathered brick walls and watchtower overlooking Anping's temple-filled old streets.
Chihkan Tower (Fort Provintia)
A graceful pair of Qing-era pavilions rising from 1653 Dutch foundations, Tainan's most storied landmark, glowing lantern-red after dark.
Anping Tree House
A former warehouse swallowed whole by banyan roots, an atmospheric ruin where walkways thread through curtains of aerial roots and dappled light.
Tainan Confucius Temple
Taiwan's first Confucian temple, founded in 1665, a serene compound of vermilion halls and ancient trees known as the island's 'First Academy'.
Shennong Street
Tainan's most photogenic lane, a narrow Qing-dynasty street of lantern-strung old houses now filled with craft studios, bars and temple incense.
Grand Mazu Temple
A former Ming princely palace converted into Taiwan's first officially sanctioned Mazu temple, rich with gold-faced statues and swallowtail roofs.
Koxinga Shrine
An elegant shrine honouring Ming loyalist Koxinga, who expelled the Dutch in 1662, set among plum trees and arched galleries.
Sicao Green Tunnel
A dreamlike mangrove canal in Taijiang National Park, where flat-bottomed boats glide beneath an arching canopy mirrored perfectly in still water.
Hayashi Department Store
A lovingly restored 1932 Japanese-era department store with a rooftop Shinto shrine, blending retro elevators, crafts and colonial nostalgia.
Garden Night Market (Huayuan)
Tainan's famous weekend-only night market, a sea of yellow banners where hundreds of stalls serve the food capital's legendary snacks.

train.note: Tainan has two stations and two entirely separate ticketing systems: TRA's Tainan Station sits in the centre beside the old city, while the THSR station is out at Guiren about 12 km southeast, linked by the TRA Shalun branch shuttle in around 25 minutes or a taxi for roughly NT$400. THSR covers Taipei in about 1 hour 45 minutes and Zuoying (Kaohsiung) in under 20, whereas TRA trains are slower but leave you downtown and run to Kaohsiung every few minutes for NT$70-100. THSR seats open 28 days ahead and the cheap early-bird tickets vanish quickly; TRA reservations open about two weeks out. Taiwan has no international rail link, so onward travel abroad is by air.

bus.note: Intercity coaches use the terminals ringing the north side of Tainan railway station. Kuo-Kuang Motor Transport, Ho-Hsin Bus and UBus run frequent services to Taipei in roughly 4-4.5 hours, plus Kaohsiung, Chiayi and Taichung, with cheap overnight departures to Taipei; tickets are bought at the counter or paid with an EasyCard/iPASS on board. Coaches undercut the high-speed train substantially on price but take more than twice as long. Being an island, Taiwan has no international bus routes at all.

ferry.note: Anping Port, 6 km west of the centre, is a fishing and small-cargo harbour with no scheduled passenger ferry - the boats there are canal cruises around the Anping and Sicao mangrove waterways. Tainan's Jiangjun and Beimen harbours handle only local fishing and excursion craft. For the Penghu islands take the summer ferry from Budai in Chiayi, about an hour north, with a crossing of roughly 90 minutes, or the year-round Taihua ferry from Kaohsiung run by Taiwan Navigation, also about an hour away by train.

half.name: Guanziling
half.blurb: Hot spring town in the hills known for its rare mud-infused, grey-colored mineral water.

half.name: Kaohsiung
half.blurb: Taiwan's major southern port city with a harborside promenade and a hillside cable car.

half.name: Wushantou Reservoir
half.blurb: Irrigation lake also called Coral Lake for its jagged, coral-like shoreline of small inlets.

full.name: Alishan National Scenic Area
full.blurb: Mountain forest park known for sunrise viewpoints, cypress trees, and a narrow-gauge mountain railway.
